title: Signature trust anchors, Windows store, RFC 3161 timestamps and revocation
acceptance: cargo test -p pdfxi-security; chain trust returns Some(true) only for a real anchor, the Windows store enumerates identities, a deterministic RFC 3161 fixture validates with a typed offline result, and revocation returns typed reasons without unbounded network calls in fast tests
notes: Home for the signature work deferred when T-0249 was narrowed this round to the PFX identity path. Trust anchors: load a PEM/DER trust-anchor bundle and build certificate paths so certificate_chain_trusted() can return Some(true) only when the signer chains to a real configured anchor, Some(false) when it does not, and None when no anchors are configured. Windows certificate store: enumerate identities with private-key handles; the FFI must be isolated (its own module with a documented unsafe boundary and forbid->deny change plus an evidence note, or a separate crate), and tests must not depend on a particular machine's store. RFC 3161: timestamp request and token validation against a deterministic fixture, returning a typed offline result when no TSA is reachable. Revocation: CRL and OCSP with typed reasons (good, revoked, unknown, unavailable) and no unbounded network calls in fast tests. Not required to tick A-20 while T-0245 shows identity and trust honestly as unverified, but required for the plan's signature-validation scope. No matrix promotion until T-0245 exposes the results.
